correctness.rationale: The characteristic polynomial trace/determinant conditions force b1k1=a²/(a−d), b2k2=−d²/(a−d) for every admissible b. With x=b1², squared gain equals [a⁴/x+d⁴/(1−x)]/(a−d)², minimized exactly at x=a²/(a²+d²) by Cauchy. Nilpotent nonzero 2×2 closed loop is rank one, so spectral norm equals Frobenius norm. Its squared norm equals [a²(1−x)+d²x]²/[x(1−x)(a−d)²], minimized at the SAME x using [a√(1−x)−d√x]²≥0. Exact rational witness a=4/5,d=3/5,b=(4/5,3/5),k=(4,−3) gives a nilpotent matrix (12/5)[[-1,1],[-1,1]] with spectral norm 24/5 and gain norm5; algebra independently checked on rational values. Blow-up is at fixed coalescence s∈(0,1); no universality for diagonalization by nonorthogonal similarities.
residual_risks: No extension is proved for nonnormal coordinates or higher-dimensional control systems.

checked_sources: Schmid et al fixed-input pole placement arXiv:1405.1516
value.rationale: Two-step deadbeat pole placement is a natural minimal control objective and nonnormal transient amplification is a distinct practical criterion. Solving the first nontrivial continuous actuator-direction co-design determines a previously unstated common optimizer and exact reciprocal-gap blow-up. The result supplies a precise counterintuition: zero closed-loop poles and minimum gain do not prevent a factor-24/5 one-step amplification for a stable open-loop plant. It is motivated structural optimization rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
residual_risks: Minimal two-mode diagonal setting only; not a general input design theorem.

final_claim: For real diag(a,d), 0<d<a<1, freely oriented unit scalar actuator b with b1 b2≠0 and feedback u=−kᵀx with both closed-loop poles zero, the unique actuator squared components a²/(a²+d²), d²/(a²+d²) simultaneously minimize ||k||₂=(a²+d²)/(a−d) and ||A−bkᵀ||₂=2ad/(a−d); both blow up as modes coalesce at fixed positive value.
limitations: Only stable diagonal two-mode real plants with distinct positive modes; Euclidean modal coordinate norms and unit actuator.
No observer, uncertainty, noise, saturation or more than two states.
